data.abstract: As one of the key components in the design and application of transformers, the insulation performance of transformer bushings directly affects the safe and stable operation of the power system. Due to the long-term influence of multiple factors such as electrical stress, load fluctuations, and environmental conditions on transformer bushings, their actual application performance is likely to gradually deteriorate, and there is a potential risk of failure during system operation. Therefore, based on the research results of the application of online monitoring technology for the insulation performance of power plant transformer bushings in recent years, the principle and corresponding method schemes of online monitoring for the insulation performance of power plant transformer bushings have been clarified. Combined with practical cases, the application effects of software and hardware have been verified, thereby providing technical support for the management of power systems in the new era.

data.abstract: Transformer bushings are an essential component of electrical transformers. It provides electrical insulation and mechanical support for the high-voltage connections within a transformer while protecting them from environmental factors like dust and moisture. According to CIGRE TB 642 in 2015, 14% of power transformer failures are caused by defective bushings. A symptom of the transformer bushing failure was detected at IBT $150 / 70 \mathrm{kV}$, owned by PLN UIT JBT. Comprehensive diagnostic testing, including tan delta and Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA), revealed a deterioration in the bushing’s insulation properties, accompanied by evidence of thermal and electrical faults. The tangent delta (dissipation factor) test results for the IBT $150 / 70 \mathrm{kV}$, phase S, indicated a value of 1.63%, which exceeds the acceptable standard. Consequently, replacement of the bushing is required immediately. The availability and condition of spare materials within PLN may not consistently meet operational needs. A dimensional mismatch was observed between the existing bushing, ABB type GOB 650 LF123-192, and the replacement bushing, ABB type GOB 650 LF123-073. If the new bushing is installed without modification, the insulation distance between the high-voltage zone and ground will be too close, causing an increased risk of electrical discharge. To resolve this issue, modifications were made to the ABB type GOB 650 LF123-073 bushing by installing an adapter in the bushing chamber. Subsequent to the modified installation of the transformer bushing, a comprehensive monitoring program was implemented, incorporating thermal image, tan delta, and capacitance testing. The results of these tests confirmed that the bushing was functioning satisfactorily.

data.abstract: This paper gives examples of the application of condition monitoring to large power transformers. In many reported cases of condition monitoring the analysis of data, conclusions drawn, and decisions made are fairly straightforward. We show such a ‘straightforward’ case relating to traditional dissolved gas analysis (DGA), but we also show cases where more analysis of the context of the main tank partial discharge (PD) measurements and bushing power factor measurements are needed to draw appropriate and actionable conclusions. Condition monitoring may provide significant benefits if data is evaluated in context, and if it is considered as part of, and embedded in, the operational and asset management processes of the organization in order to ensure positive outcomes.

data.abstract: This paper presents the development of on-line monitoring for condenser type bushing of power transformer in order to detect a degradation of bushing and to provide the alarm before bushing failure. For the bushing degradation analysis, the capacitance and power factor of bushing internal insulation are on-line monitored and measured by installing the sensing device at the test tap of bushing. The changing of internal insulation capacitance leads to the change of voltage across tap capacitor and the change of leakage current through bushing insulation at the test tab. Such changes result in the change of power factor or phase angle of leakage current. Thus, the leakage current is additionally detected by installing the Hall Effect sensing device to observe the trend of bushing failure. A total of eight cases of both normal and degraded insulation are investigated. The internal insulation capacitance as well as the magnitude and phase angle of three phase leakage current were measured and compared with the commissioning value or observed the increasing trend to set the alarm level. In case of degraded bushing, the leakage currents changed and caused the summation of leakage current value to be greater than the standard value. Then the alarm is activated. This knowledge was used to develop the detection and decision making algorithms in LabVIEW program to determine the condition of transformer bushing.
